body: Celtic 0-0 Ferencvaros. Martin O’Neill was in a foul mood before the game; he’d have been properly fuming had Adam Bagi met Bamidele Yusuf’s fine inswinger from the right with the header it deserved. Wide and high.

GOAL! Juventus 1-0 NEC (Gonzalez 9). Two-time European champions Juventus will feel they’re slumming it ever so slightly in the Europa. Nicolas Gonzalez gives them the fast start they’ll have been expecting.

Adrien Truffert is sent scampering down the left. He crosses low. Justin Kluivert times his run perfectly, opening his body and flicking into the bottom left. A simple move, crisply executed. The offside flag goes up, but VAR gets involved and the man who took Bournemouth’s first kick in European football gets their first goal too!

Terry Yegbe takes a throw from the Poznan left touchline. Across the face of his own box. It’s a suicidal effort. Yeremy Pino intercepts, and he’s clean through down the middle. Pino enters the box and steers a shot across the keeper and into the bottom left. Selhurst Park erupts!

articles.title: McIlroy falters as Rai shares lead at Wentworth
articles.summary: Aaron Rai shoots a six-under 66 to share the first-round lead with Sweden's Joakim Lagergren at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth as Rory McIlroy suffers a late stumble.
body: While Rory McIlroy sparkled and then suffered a late stumble, Aaron Rai was a model of consistency as he shot a six-under 66 to share the first-round lead with Sweden's Joakim Lagergren at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

Rai, who became England's most recent major winner earlier this season, knocked in seven birdies, with the only blemish to his card arriving on the 16th, when he found the fairway bunker off the tee and ended with a bogey five.
Lagergren, whose one and only win on the DP World Tour was back in 2018, also made a fine start with an eagle on the 12th, the highlight of his round.
Six-time major winner McIlroy had got under way in sensational fashion earlier in the day until his round unravelled on the back nine.

articles.title: Northants require record run chase to beat Derbys
articles.summary: Nick Potts' maiden half-century rescues Derbyshire as they threaten to derail Northamptonshire's promotion challenge in the County Championship.
body: Derbyshire were struggling at 177-7, despite Martin Andersson's 62, when Potts – drafted in the previous day as an injury replacement for Ben Aitchison – joined forces with fellow seamer Brett Randell.

The eighth-wicket pair shared a partnership of 99, with Potts hitting 57 and Randell 45 to stretch the total to 286 and set the home side a target of 349, which would be a county record fourth-innings chase against Derbyshire.
Northamptonshire, whose openers reached 37 without loss at stumps, need a victory to regain second place in the table from promotion rivals Kent going into next week's final round of fixtures.

Despite an early morning shower, Derbyshire's second innings began on time and Harry Came was fortunate to avoid a pair, steering Harry Conway low to third slip where George Bartlett shelled the chance.

articles.title: Abhishek hits fastest century in full-member T20s
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma hits a 30-ball century - the fastest in a T20 international between two full-member nations - in India's third T20 against Afghanistan.
body: Abhishek Sharma hit a 30-ball century - the fastest in a T20 international between two full-member nations - in India's 127-run victory in the third T20 against Afghanistan in Delhi.
Opener Abhishek, who was knocked off the top of the T20 batting rankings in July, continued to make 108 from 34 balls, hitting nine fours and 11 sixes in India's 221-7.
The 26-year-old reached three figures in the ninth over - at that stage India were 132-0 - having scored a remarkable 96 of his 100 runs in boundaries.
The only exceptions were the single to get to his hundred, another in the previous over and a two in the third.

articles.title: 'Ton of respect for' Holly: Steve Sarkisian on curt interview, Arch Manning's Rowe comment
articles.summary: Texas Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian said he could have handled postgame interview with Holly Rowe better, which could have avoided Arch Manning controversy
body: Days after Texas football star Arch Manning ignited a social media firestorm by laughing at an AI-generated video of his coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe, Sarkisian said, "Arch recognizes he made a mistake, and it's an unfortunate one."

"Nowhere do we condone domestic violence or violence against women," Sarkisian said Thursday during his weekly Zoom meeting with the media. "Nothing in our program says that. I think if (Arch) could take it back, he would. He has since apologized to Holly. He's made a public apology, and our goal is that we can move forward and him be the guy that that we all know that he is and what he represents."

The fake video after the Longhorns' 24-23 comeback win over Ohio State spoofed a postgame interaction between Sarkisian and Rowe, ending with the journalist being struck in the face. A reporter asked Monday if Manning had seen any online videos that had been posted about Saturday night's postgame scene at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Manning said he had seen an AI-edited video about the abrupt interview between Sarkisian and Rowe.

"There's just so many different narratives and so many different opinions and speculations," Tatum said on the Dan Patrick Show. "For me, I love that guy. What we were able to accomplish together in nine years — we went to the Conference Finals five times, we went to the championships twice, we won a championship, we've shared All-Star Games together. You can't talk about him without talking about him, and vice versa. The success that we've had as two young kids growing up in this league and really just pushing each other.

articles.title: Somerset's title hopes hit while Stokes stars with ball for Durham
articles.summary: Dom Bess dented the Rothesay County Championship title hopes of old club Somerset after he struck 77 for Yorkshire to set a tricky final-day victory target of 287.
body: Spinner Bess walked to the crease with Yorkshire on 54-6 and after he joined forces with George Hill to take the hosts up to 128 at the end of day two, the duo kicked on during the morning session and put on 166 for the seventh wicket.

Hill narrowly missed out on a century with 89 before Bess was out for 77, which helped Yorkshire up to 275 before Somerset were reduced to 73-3 during a rain-affected chase, with a further 214 runs required to reclaim top spot.

Warwickshire's two-day triumph over Essex has sent them to the Division One summit, but the three-way title race may become a two-horse race after Nottinghamshire collapsed in their second innings at Hove.

After Nottinghamshire dismissed Sussex for 358 and crucially claimed a third bowling point off the last ball of the 110th over, Haseeb Hameed's team were undone by the bowling of Aristides Karvelas and Jaydev Unadkhat.

articles.title: Will Palmer, Foden and Trent be recalled to England squad?
articles.summary: Cole Palmer's outstanding form this season has put him in a strong position for an England recall, with the Chelsea man the most likely to be included from all the big names left out of the World Cup squad.
body: Thomas Tuchel is set to name his first England squad since the World Cup on Friday; having stated publicly that England's DNA does not allow for ball-retaining passers, can he continue to leave the likes of Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold out?

Palmer, along with Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold, was a headline omission from Thomas Tuchel's tournament squad in May, but he is one of the most startlingly in-form players in the Premier League right now, and the smart money is on him winning his international place back.

Two goals and two assists show that. Only his team-mate Joao Pedro has more in the Premier League so far this season and only Bruno Fernandes has created more chances and had more shots combined (25) than Palmer (24).

It also feels like a space may have opened up for Palmer, with Eze's indifferent form for Arsenal. While starting in Europe and the Carabao Cup, Eze has yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.
